parts.title: Starting again
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I started learning the violin when I was seven, and for years I loved it. My teacher, Mrs Okafor, was strict but kind, and she always said that practice made a musician. By the age of twelve, I was playing in the school orchestra. Then, one day, I stopped.

It happened slowly. My friends were going to the park after school while I stayed at home with my violin. I told myself that I was tired, and then that I was too busy. Every Thursday I walked to my lesson with a heavy heart. Mrs Okafor never complained. She just asked, 'Are you still enjoying it?' and, one day, I said that I was not. I think we were both sad, but she said she understood.

For two years, the violin stayed in its case under my bed. Then my grandmother had a birthday, and my mother asked me to play her favourite song. I was terrified, because I had not touched the instrument since the summer before. My fingers had forgotten the notes and I made a lot of mistakes. But my grandmother clapped as if I were a famous performer, and something inside me changed.

I now play for fun, not for exams. I practise when I want to, and I have joined a small group that meets on Saturdays. It is nothing like my old orchestra, but I enjoy every minute of it.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel about the violin when she was young?
options: She was afraid of her teacher.
She thought it was too hard.
questions.explanation: She says that for years she loved the violin and Mrs Okafor was strict but kind.

options: She lost interest and wanted free time.

options: She asked her parents to talk to her.
questions.explanation: She said she understood, though both of them were sad.

parts.title: A street musician
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Every weekday morning, at half past eight, Tomas opens his guitar case at the corner of the market square and starts to play. He is nineteen, and he has been a street musician for two years. [1] Some people stop to listen, and a few of them leave a coin or two.

Tomas did not plan to be a busker. He studied music at college, but he found it hard to get work after he finished. [2] He decided to play outside, just to practise, and to his surprise, people liked it.

The job is not as easy as it looks. In winter, his fingers get so cold that he can hardly move them. [3] Rain is the worst problem, because he cannot play at all, and he goes home with no money.

However, there are also moments that he will never forget. A few months ago, a small girl danced in front of him for ten minutes. [4] Another time, an old man told him that his song had reminded him of his wife.

Tomas hopes to record an album one day. [5] "Meanwhile," he says with a smile, "the square is my concert hall."
sentences: Tomas likes playing the piano more than the guitar.
He uses an old guitar that once belonged to his uncle.
Her parents had to carry her away when the song finished.
He wears thick gloves with the tips cut off, but it is still difficult.
Some of them gave him a lot of money.
He has already written about twelve songs for it.
He needed money, and the only free place to try was the street.
Many people who pass are on their way to work and do not have much time.

gaps.explanation: The people who pass on their way to work are introduced before "Some people stop to listen".
"He found it hard to get work" leads to needing money and using the street as a place to play; the next sentence says he decided to play outside.
"His fingers get so cold" is followed by the gloves with the tips cut off, and then the worst problem is rain.
The girl dancing for ten minutes continues with the parents carrying her away when the song finished.
"Tomas hopes to record an album" is followed by the songs he has written for it; then "Meanwhile" introduces his present concert hall.

parts.title: Music and mood
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Many people listen to music every day, but did you know that it can change the way you feel? Scientists have found that slow, quiet music can help you to [1] after a stressful day, while fast music with a strong beat can give you more energy when you exercise. Music can also bring back memories. When we hear a song from our childhood, we [2] remember places and people that we thought we had forgotten. Some schools now play soft music in the corridors because it makes students feel calmer. Others ask them to [3] their favourite tracks to share in class. Of course, not everyone enjoys the same kind of music, and a song that makes you happy may [4] your friend feel sad. This is why it is so important to [5] attention to how music makes you feel. If a song makes you uncomfortable, you can always choose [6].

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: Slow music helps you to relax after a stressful day.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: A familiar song can "suddenly" bring back memories; "seldom", "never" and "rarely" do not fit the idea of remembering.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: Students are asked to bring favourite tracks to school to share.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "Make your friend feel sad" is the correct structure: make + object + base form.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Pay attention to" is the fixed expression.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "Choose another" (song) completes the sentence.

parts.title: An invitation to a concert
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Hi Lena,
Guess what? My brother's band is playing at the youth centre this Saturday, and I have two free tickets! The concert starts [1] seven o'clock, but the doors open at half past six. You do not have to bring anything with you, [2] there is a café inside. Last time they played, I enjoyed it so much [3] I bought their record afterwards. Would you like to come? If you want, we could have something to eat before the show. I [4] ask my mum to give us a lift, so we will not have to take the bus. Please let me know [5] Thursday, because I need to tell my brother how many people are coming. It will be great [6] you can come!
Beatrix

gaps.explanation: We use "at" with a clock time: at seven o'clock.
"Because" gives the reason why she does not need to bring anything.
"So much that" shows the result of enjoying the concert.
A modal expresses the plan or possibility of asking her mum.
"By Thursday" means no later than Thursday.
"It will be great if you can come" is a conditional hope.

parts.title: Short conversations

turns.speaker: beaumont
turns.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Greenfield School spring concert. The doors are open now. The concert will start at seven o’clock, and the ushers will begin to close the doors at five to seven. For this reason, we ask everybody to be in your seats by a quarter to seven. If you arrive after that, you will have to wait outside until the first song finishes. The doors opened at half past six, so you have had plenty of time. Please switch off your phones, and enjoy the music.

turns.speaker: hadrian

I could phone Marcus and ask if he wants to go to the cinema, but he’s at his grandmother’s this week, so that’s a no. Instead, I’ve decided to stay at home and put some new songs on my phone. The band you told me about has an album, and I want to hear it before Saturday. Have a great time tonight!

turns.speaker: gawain

turns.speaker: winona_x
turns.text: Something modern, like a pop song. Everyone will recognise it.

turns.speaker: ignatz

turns.speaker: winona_x

turns.speaker: rhiannon

parts.title: A talk about a music camp
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Welcome, everyone, to the Brindle Summer Music Camp. I’m Ferdinand, the camp leader. The camp lasts for five days, and it begins on Monday at nine o’clock. I know that some of you hoped for a whole week, but the college needs the rooms at the weekend. Let me tell you the plan. In the mornings we have lessons in small groups. Many of you asked for private lessons, but there aren’t enough teachers, so you will be in groups of four. This is actually better, because you learn from the others. In the afternoons you can choose between singing, drums and the orchestra. On Wednesday we’re going on a special trip. You might expect a visit to a concert hall, but we’re going to a recording studio in the city. A producer will show you how bands record an album, and you’ll be allowed to try the equipment. We’ll go by bus after breakfast and come back by four. The highlight of the week is our final concert. We used to hold it in the afternoon, but the parents asked for a later time, so it takes place on Friday evening, in the main hall. Your family and friends are welcome, and there’ll be tea and cake. Now, some practical things. The camp provides lunch, and there are water fountains everywhere, but please bring your own water bottle, and don’t forget to write your name on it. You don’t need to bring your own instrument, except for the guitarists. Lastly, the price. The full course used to cost eighty pounds, but this year it is only sixty, because the town council helps us. You can pay by card or in cash at the office. I look forward to meeting you all on Monday morning. Thank you!

gaps.explanation: The camp lasts five days; the college needs the rooms at the weekend.

gaps.prompt: There are no private lessons; students learn in small ___
gaps.explanation: Private lessons were not possible; students are in groups of four.

gaps.prompt: The Wednesday trip is to a place where bands make albums: a ___
gaps.explanation: They go to a recording studio, not a concert hall.

gaps.prompt: The parents asked for the final concert to be on Friday ___
gaps.explanation: It used to be in the afternoon; it is now on Friday evening.

gaps.prompt: Students should write their name on their ___
gaps.explanation: The camp provides lunch and fountains, but they bring a water bottle.

parts.title: An interview with a young drummer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Sigrun, you’re only seventeen and you play drums in two bands. How did you get interested?

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: My father took me to a concert when I was eight, and it was amazing, but I didn’t think about drums then. No teacher suggested it either. The real start was at home, in the kitchen. I was about five, and I took the pots and pans from the cupboard and played them with wooden spoons for hours. My mum still remembers the noise, and she says she never found some of the spoons.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How did you learn your skills?

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: I had weekly lessons for a year, but I found them slow and I stopped. And I can’t read music well, so the books didn’t help. What worked was the internet. I watched videos of other drummers, then paused them, and copied the movements until I got them right. I learned a lot that way.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People think the drummer just makes the noise. Is that true?

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: Not at all. Some say it’s the easiest job, but it isn’t, and I don’t think it’s the most famous one either, because the singer gets all the attention. What a drummer does is keep the time, so everyone plays together. If I make a mistake, the whole band falls apart.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Has anything funny happened at a concert? Tell us about it.

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: Oh yes. Last year, in the middle of a fast song, I lost one of my sticks. It flew across the stage and hit the guitarist, who thought it was a bird! I forgot a song once, but that was a rehearsal. And the power cut was during another show, but it didn’t affect us.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How do your parents feel about the noise at home?

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: My parents were very patient, but the neighbours weren’t. They didn’t move house, because they couldn’t afford it, and they didn’t tell me to play less either. My dad built a little room at the end of the garden with thick walls and special foam. It’s like a small studio, and now I can practise all evening.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Last question. What would you like to do in the future?

turns.speaker: sigrun
turns.text: I’d like to study music at university, and later maybe teach children. I’m no good as a singer, believe me. Travelling would be nice, and I’ll probably do that with the band, but it’s not the main plan. I want to share what I love, and to show other girls that the drums are not only for boys. That matters a lot to me.

questions.prompt: How did Sigrun first become interested in drums?
options: She saw a concert with her father.
She played in the kitchen as a child.
A teacher asked her to try them.
questions.explanation: Her father took her to a concert at eight and no teacher suggested drums; she began in the kitchen with pots and pans at five.

questions.prompt: How did she learn most of her skills?
options: By going to lessons every week
questions.explanation: Lessons were slow and books were no help; she learned by watching other drummers online and copying them.

questions.prompt: What does she say about the role of the drummer?
options: It keeps the whole band together.
It is the most famous job in the band.
It is the easiest job in the band.
questions.explanation: It is not the easiest or the most famous job; the drummer keeps the time so that everyone plays together.

questions.prompt: What happened at a concert last year?
questions.explanation: The power cut was another show and the forgotten song was a rehearsal; at the concert, her stick flew across the stage.

questions.prompt: What solution did her parents find for the noise?
options: They moved to a bigger house.
They built a practice room outside.
They asked her to play less.
questions.explanation: They did not move house and did not tell her to play less; her dad built a little room at the end of the garden.

questions.prompt: What does Sigrun hope to do in the future?
questions.explanation: She wants to study music and later teach children; travel is not the main plan and she is no good as a singer.
